$$
R_{2}:=R_{2}+\left(3\right)R_{1}\qquad M\sim \left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & 2 & 3 & 4 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 0 \\ 2 & 5 & 6 & 12\end{array}\right]

$$

$$

$$

$$
R_{1}:=R_{1}+\left(-2\right)R_{2}\qquad M\sim \left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & 0 & 3 & -4 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 & 4 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 0\end{array}\right]
$$

The corresponding system is now

$$
\left\{\begin{aligned}x + 3 z &=-4 \\ y &=4 \\ 0 &=0\end{aligned}\right.
$$

The final equation is $0=0$, so it imposes no restriction. The basic variables are $x$ and $y$, and the free variable is $z$. Find $x$ and $y$ in terms of $z$. Therefore, the general solution is

$$
\left\{\begin{aligned}x &=- 3 z - 4 \\ y &=4 \\ z &=z\end{aligned}\right.
$$

$$
\begin{bmatrix}x \\ y \\ z\end{bmatrix}=\begin{bmatrix}- 3 z - 4 \\ 4 \\ z\end{bmatrix},\,z\in (-\infty ,\infty )
$$

R_{1}\leftrightarrow R_{2}\qquad M\sim \left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & -1 & -3 & -7 \\ 2 & -1 & -5 & -11 \\ 0 & 2 & 2 & 6\end{array}\right]
$$



$$
R_{2}:=R_{2}+\left(-2\right)R_{1}\qquad M\sim \left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & -1 & -3 & -7 \\ 0 & 1 & 1 & 3 \\ 0 & 2 & 2 & 6\end{array}\right]
$$



$$
R_{3}:=R_{3}+\left(-2\right)R_{2}\qquad M\sim \left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & -1 & -3 & -7 \\ 0 & 1 & 1 & 3 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 0\end{array}\right]
$$

In the row echelon form above, we have only two pivots (in the $1$st and $2$nd columns). To transform the matrix to reduced row echelon form, we need to create zeros above the pivots only.

$$
R_{1}:=R_{1}+\left(1\right)R_{2}\qquad M\sim \left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & 0 & -2 & -4 \\ 0 & 1 & 1 & 3 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 0\end{array}\right]
$$

The corresponding system is now

$$
\left\{\begin{aligned}x - 2 z &=-4 \\ y + z &=3 \\ 0 &=0\end{aligned}\right.
$$

The final equation is $0=0$, so it imposes no restriction. The basic variables are $x$ and $y$, and the free variable is $z$. Find $x$ and $y$ in terms of $z$. Therefore, the general solution is

$$
\left\{\begin{aligned}x &=2 z - 4 \\ y &=3 - z \\ z &=z\end{aligned}\right.
$$

where $z$ is an arbitrary real number. In vector form, the solution can be written as

$$
\begin{bmatrix}x \\ y \\ z\end{bmatrix}=\begin{bmatrix}2 z - 4 \\ 3 - z \\ z\end{bmatrix},\,z\in (-\infty ,\infty )
$$
